question_en:
The community image archive has received the batch of removable storage media shown in the photographs and needs to assign digitization stations based on the required reading devices. Media that require matching floppy drives, tape drives, or original proprietary mechanisms to read should go to the "Dedicated Legacy Equipment Station"; media readable via common USB interfaces, card readers, or compatible optical drives should go to the "Common Interface Workstation". Please answer the following questions:

1. What media items appear individually in the photographs? What reading mechanism or interface does each item require? Please list them in a table. Which media items should go to the "Dedicated Legacy Equipment Station"? Which should go to the "Common Interface Workstation"?

The answer must include a "Media—Reading Mechanism or Interface—Station" table, followed by separate lists of the media items assigned to each of the two stations.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · 1-1-F01

## Step 01 · inspect_image / Determine Input and Full Scope

Action: Open the only current input image in this problem's images, and register each item one by one in the order shown in the image.

Evidence Observation (Archival Evidence Summary): The image contains a total of 13 physical media items: three floppy disks of different specifications, one compact cassette, one 8 mm data tape, one USB flash drive, one CF card, one SDHC card, three stacked Microdrives, one DVD+RW, and one CD-R. Transparent protective cases are not counted separately; the three Microdrives are counted individually.

Result of this step: Set the scope to 13 items; complete full registration first, then filter or calculate.

## Step 02 · parse_task / Establish Fields to Check and Output Constraints

Action: Read question_zh-new, dividing information confirmable from the image and information that must be looked up externally.

Evidence Observation (Archival Evidence Summary): Route based on required reading mechanism/interface, not by year, size, or capacity. Even if a 3.5-inch floppy drive can connect to a computer via USB, the medium still requires a floppy drive to read; per this problem, it belongs to the Dedicated Legacy Equipment Station.

Result of this step: Subsequent web searches are only to fill in these fields; finally, output strictly according to the requirements at the end of the question.

## Step 03 · reverse_image_lookup / Locate Photos and Verify Object Types

Action: Example query: "Forty years of Removable Storage"; open the Commons description page and the original image, compare the positions and readable labels of the 13 media items.

Evidence Observation (Archival Evidence Summary): The photo description discusses 11 types of technology, but there are 3 physical Microdrive items, so the input members total 13. Collection/standard links are used to explain formats and reading methods; they do not automatically prove that each branded item in the photo is that specific collection artifact.
